facts: This is an appeal by special leave against the judgment dated September 12, 1969, of a Single Judge of the High Court of Allahabad accepting an application u/s. 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure, setting aside the orders of the courts below and directing that the application made by the defendant u/s. 34 of the Arbitration Act shall stand rejected so that the suit would proceed.

The suit out of which this appeal has arisen was filed by the respondent before us for recovery of Rs. 2, 000 on account of dues recoverable from the irrigation Department of the petitioner State for work done by the plaintiff in pursuance of an agreement, Cl. 22 of which runs thus,Except where otherwise specified in the contract the decision of the Superintending Engineer for the time being shall be final, conclusive and binding on all parties to the contract upon all questions relating to the meaning of the specifications, design, drawing and instructions hereinbefore mentioned.

The defendant-respondent made an application u/s. 34 of the Arbitration Act to the trial Court on the plea that the above extracted Cl. 22 amounted to an arbitration agreement. The pleas found favour with the trial Court as well as the appellate court but was rejected by the High Court in revision on the ground that it merely conferred power on the Superintending Engineer to take decisions on his own and that it did not authorise the parties to refer any matter to his arbitration.
In this connection the High Court particularly adverted to the marginal note to the said clause which was to the following effectDirection of work.
issues: What is the nature of Clause 22?
Does it amount to an arbitration agreement?
petitioner_arguments: Mr. Dixit relied on Governor-General v. Simla Banking and Industrial Company Ltd. 1947 AIR(Lah) 215 : 226 IC 444, Dewan Chand v. State of Jammu and Kashmir (AIR 1961 J&K 58) and Ram Lal v. Punjab State 1966 AIR(P&H) 436 : 68 Punj LR 522 : 1966 (2) ILR(P&H) 428 )
court_reasoning: The purpose of the clause clearly appears to be to vest the Superintending Engineer with supervision of the execution of the work and administrative control over it from time to time.

As pointed out by the High Court such a clause can be interpreted only as one conferring power on the Superintending Engineer to take decisions all by himself and not by reason of any reference which the parties might make to him.
The language of this clause is materially different from the clause in the present case and in our opinion was correctly interpreted as amounting to an arbitration agreement.
holding: Holding, in conformity with the judgment of the High Court, that Cl. 22 above extracted does not amount to an arbitration agreement, we find no force in this appeal which is dismissed with costs.
cases_cited: Dewan Chand v. State of Jammu
Mr. Dixit relied on Governor-General v. Simla Banking
